Method of Attack: Targets Android devices to take over local WiFi routers and hijack web traffic
Collects user's WiFi network information after infecting device
Sends info to public C&C server to determine ISP and DNS records
Brute-forces local WiFi routers using default admin credentials (successful mainly on TP-Link routers)
Modifies router's DNS settings to malicious IP addresses from C&C server
Sets secondary DNS to 8.8.8.8 to maintain internet connection if malicious DNS goes down
Hijacks DNS to redirect users to phishing sites to steal credentials
Indicators of Compromise: Default admin credentials list used for brute forcing routers
Secondary DNS set to 8.8.8.8 (Google public DNS)
Public C&C server accessible with evidence of 1,280 infected routers
